interpretation: Across the eligible NPS Tier-3 panel, binary Zostera presence and focal frequency are saturated while quantitative cover varies substantially and declines on average within repeated transects. This independently reproduces the ecological-state-decoupling pattern at a different species and monitoring network, but it is post-hoc and is not an independent predictive validation of the Tampa early-warning endpoint.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc because the NPS response was already opened by the frozen v2 estimability test.
Not counted as independent predictive confirmation of the Tampa early-warning endpoint.
Recorded presence refers to observation in re-observed seagrass-bearing quadrats, not total meadow occupancy.
Cover trends are observational and do not identify nutrient, temperature, or climate causation.
Location-specific slopes are descriptive and show substantial spatial heterogeneity, including positive cover trend at Moriches Bay.
